newsitem.title: USA: Powell hopes service summit will unite Americans.
newsitem.headline: Powell hopes service summit will unite Americans.

text.p: Retired Gen. Colin Powell said Monday he hoped a national service summit in Philadelphia next week would help unite Americans across race and class divides and ease tensions that are tearing the country apart.

Powell is general chairman of The Presidents' Summit for America's Future, a non-partisan summit which President Clinton has described as an unprecedented national summons to service and volunteerism.
"The arguments from one side to the other have become a little too sharp, a little too divisive," Powell told NBC-TV's "Nightly News with Tom Brokaw" Monday.
"I hope that this summit gives us the opportunity to start ... talking more softly to one another," the former chairman of the joint chiefs of staff said.
The summit is scheduled for April 27-29 in Philadelphia.

"Remember, we're all in this together. We're all part of the same family. You may be black; I may be white. You may be rich; you may be poor. But we're all Americans, and we've got to share with each other and care for each other."

Powell said volunteering made good sense for corporations, individuals and non-profit groups. The summit was intended to spur more Americans to get involved in community service as a way to help disadvantaged people.
"I think one of the single greatest threats is the fact that there are more and more young Americans who are getting left on the wrong side of the economic divide in America," Powell said.
He said the divide was growing and many young people were wondering "whether or not there is a place for them in America after the year 2000."
The charismatic and popular former military chief again rejected speculation that he was using the service summit as a platform to launch a presidential campaign for 2000.
"I'm turning my back on politics and remaining in private life," he said.
